title: Ala al-Din Abu al-Shamat
summary: Ala al-Din Abu al-Shamat was the beloved son of the chief merchant of Cairo. Raised in piety, trade, and horsemanship, he embarked with his father’s blessing on a great merchant...
full_text:
Ala al-Din Abu al-Shamat was the beloved son of the chief merchant of Cairo. Raised in piety, trade, and horsemanship, he embarked with his father’s blessing on a great merchant caravan across the Sinai toward Baghdad.

On the road, the caravan was ambushed by desert brigands, and Ala al-Din was stripped of his goods. Alone in the desert, he placed his trust in providence, walked until he reached the gates of Baghdad, and found employment with an elderly jeweler who recognized his honesty and treated him as an adopted son.

When the old jeweler died, he bequeathed his shop and his fortune to Ala al-Din. The young merchant's prosperity, handsome countenance, and open-handed charity won the hearts of the citizens, but it also aroused the burning jealousy of Habazlam, the chief magistrate’s son, who plotted his destruction.

Habazlam stole the Caliph’s golden crown and state mantle from the imperial treasury and secretly buried them beneath the flagstones of Ala al-Din's warehouse. The city watch searched the premises, discovered the royal insignia, and dragged the innocent youth to the scaffold.

Just as the executioner raised his scimitar before the palace, Ahmad al-Danaf, the captain of the honorable vigilantes of Baghdad, burst through the crowd with evidence of Habazlam’s conspiracy. The Caliph Harun al-Rashid ordered the magistrate's son arrested, restored Ala al-Din’s honor with royal robes, and made him the chief inspector of all the markets of the empire.
moral: Divine protection shields the innocent from the most venomous conspiracies of treacherous rivals.
